title: Cerebrate Pixel 6 model catalog
description: What each model is and does: identity, capabilities, artifacts (upstream provenance plus the exact files deployed, with sha256), model-level aliases, serving interface, and task-level selections. How each configuration executes lives in models/variants.yaml (variants.schema.json); scripts/validate-model-catalog checks both together.

tasks.description: Task-level selection, separate from each model's own aliases so a task isn't tied to one architecture. Targets are immutable <model>/<variant> ids. A task with available: true must select production variants with serving for default and fallback; quality may name a validated, unserved variant.

available.description: Advertised as an available service. Requires default and fallback to be production variants with serving (validator).

capabilities.description: Public capability names, per catalog v4 Section 10 (e.g. classify-image, chat).

artifacts.description: Keyed by deployment artifact type, e.g. tflite, litertlm, onnx.

worker.description: The serving worker. Absent = no serving worker yet (validated only); such a model can't be a task's default or fallback.

execution_preferences.description: Keyed by device (e.g. pixel6), ordered most- to least-preferred backend identifiers.

residency.description: Per catalog v4 Section 9. Applied at the worker-process level, not in-process.

previous_ids.description: Former catalog keys of this model (renames), still accepted by the CLI's resolve.

aliases.description: Model-level selection aliases -> variant ids in models/variants.yaml. default = what a caller gets without asking; reference = the exact configuration closest to the original model; fast = the validated performance choice; quality = the validated quality choice; fallback = what the model degrades to. Lifecycle status lives on the variant, not here.

serving.description: The model's MLServer endpoint and its contract. Present once a variant is staged or in production.

validated.description: Keyed by device_backend, e.g. pixel6_nnapi. Measured status only -- never assumed.

api_requirements.description: Only meaningful for litertlm artifacts. Found necessary after granite-docling-258M (litert-community): its multimodal .litertlm cannot be driven through the plain C API's SessionAdvanced path at all (verified against the real LiteRT-LM source, not assumed) -- only through the full C++ SDK's InputImage(TensorBuffer) construction, or the Kotlin/Swift app layers. Recording this per-artifact so that gap isn't rediscovered per model.

litertlm_surface.description: Which integration surface(s) this artifact's modality actually requires. c_session (engine.h's plain C API) is confirmed multimodal-incapable -- it can only construct InputImage from raw encoded bytes, which SessionAdvanced's PreprocessContents rejects for anything but text. cpp_session_advanced is the verified-real, heavier full-C++-SDK path (InputImage(TensorBuffer), CMake+Abseil-cpp build, same shape as the LiteRT CompiledModel spike's C++ SDK path) that Cerebrate's existing native-worker architecture could still reach without an Android app. kotlin_conversation/swift_conversation are the model card's only currently-documented working paths, both requiring an actual app, not a native binary.

native_c_session.description: Whether this artifact's required litertlm_surface is reachable from the existing plain-C-API native worker pattern (cerebrate-generate) without further build/architecture changes.

validated.description: Whether native_c_session was actually exercised end-to-end on-device, not assumed from reading the API surface alone.

name.description: Flat device file name in /data/local/tmp (cerebrate-supervisor's staging rule); unique across the catalog.

upstream_name.description: The file's name in its source repo when it differs from name.

origin.description: Where the validated copy lives on the device today when it isn't yet staged flat (e.g. depth/depth_anything_v2_small.tflite).

files.description: The exact files this artifact deploys, as validated (sha256 of the bytes on the device). scripts/cerebrate-models check-artifacts verifies a directory or the device against them.

derived.description: true = our own conversion of the source (kept in the derived store, models/README.md); false/absent = the published files themselves.

produced_by.description: Repo path of the script that produced the derived files.

target.description: Where the files are needed: the Android host (default) or the Debian guest's adapter.

source.description: Exactly one provenance shape: a pinned repo revision (e.g. Hugging Face), or a pinned direct-download URL with a checksum.

binary.description: Which Android worker process type serves this model, e.g. cerebrate-infer, cerebrate-generate.

ram_mb.description: null where genuinely not yet measured -- do not fill in a guessed value.
